bibliography.title: Reinforced Sequential Monte Carlo for Amortised Sampling

sections.title: 2. Amortised and Particle Methods for Sampling
B. Generative Processes for Diffusion and Sequence Generation
E. Training Techniques for Diffusion Samplers
I. Application to Biochemical Sequence Design

abstract_sentences.text: This paper proposes a synergy of amortised and particle-based methods for sampling from distributions defined by unnormalised density functions.

We state a connection between sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) and neural sequential samplers trained by maximum-entropy reinforcement learning (MaxEnt RL), wherein learnt sampling policies and value functions define proposal kernels and twist functions.

evidence.anchor: policies and value functions define proposal kernels

abstract_sentences.text: Exploiting this connection, we introduce an off-policy RL training procedure for the sampler that uses samples from SMC – using the learnt sampler as a proposal – as a behaviour policy that better explores the target distribution.
We describe techniques for stable joint training of proposals and twist functions and an adaptive weight tempering scheme to reduce training signal variance.

Furthermore, building upon past attempts to use experience replay to guide the training of neural samplers, we derive a way to combine historical samples with annealed importance sampling weights within a replay buffer.

On synthetic multi-modal targets (in both continuous and discrete spaces) and the Boltzmann distribution of alanine dipeptide conformations, we demonstrate improvements in approximating the true distribution as well as training stability compared to both amortised and Monte Carlo methods.

claim_closure.claim: HVI, MaxEnt RL, and SMC/AIS can be placed in one framework.
claim_closure.evidence_response: The paper gives definitions and algebraic links, not a named theorem/proof.

claim_closure.claim: SMC samples can serve as an off-policy behaviour policy for the sampler.
claim_closure.method_response: §3.2 and Algorithms 2/4/7 generate weighted terminals then backward trajectories.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Tables 1–2 report target-specific improvements with heterogeneous metrics.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §5 says SMC informs off-policy RL design.

claim_closure.claim: Importance-weighted replay combines historical samples in a useful way.
claim_closure.method_response: §3.3 defines batch and within-batch weights in (12)–(13).
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 4 and Tables 8–9 compare prioritisation alternatives.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §5 explicitly returns to importance weights for replay.

claim_closure.claim: Stable joint proposal/flow training and adaptive tempering improve the sampler.
claim_closure.method_response: TB updates θ, chunk SubTB updates φ, and ESS chooses λ.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 3, Table 6 and Figure 7 support selected conditions; there is no general guarantee.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §5 reports substantial improvements at high level.

claim_closure.claim: The framework covers continuous, discrete, and alanine-dipeptide sampling.
claim_closure.method_response: Appendix B instantiates diffusion and prepend/append processes.
claim_closure.evidence_response: ALDP Table 7 and discrete Tables 8–9 provide application results, all after the main body.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §5 does not individually revisit all three applications.

claim_closure.claim: This is the first treatment of all three topics in one framework.
claim_closure.method_response: The paper supplies a related-work narrative, not a complete priority comparison procedure.
claim_closure.evidence_response: References and Appendix A give positioning evidence only.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §5 restates that this had not been functionally done before.

final_judgment.single_storyline: Learnt policy/flow are recast as SMC proposal/twisted targets; SMC then supplies off-policy trajectories and importance-weighted replay improves the loop. [PDF p.5 §3.1–3.3, Figure 1]
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The main body keeps the dictionary, SMC weights, training loop, two benchmark tables and two core ablations. [PDF p.2–9 §2–§5]
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Generative processes, algorithms, hyperparameters, sensitivity, ALDP and discrete results move to Appendix B–I; those application claims therefore require the appendix. [PDF p.16–30]
final_judgment.best_pattern: A three-part contribution preview, one system dataflow figure, then aggregate benchmarks followed by orthogonal ablations creates the clearest reading path. [PDF p.2, p.5, p.7–9]
final_judgment.largest_gap: There is no formal theorem/proof and some target–metric comparisons are mixed; the gradient-based GMM40 dimension is internally uncertain. [PDF p.3 §2.2; p.7 §4.1/Table 2; p.22 F.1]
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For multi-paradigm methods, first make the shared computational object explicit, then give each component an isolating result or ablation and call appendix evidence precisely. [PDF p.2–9; p.16–30]
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: Use this pattern when mappings and empirical controls are concrete; keep proof, failure analysis or deployment constraints in the main body when they bear the decision. [PDF p.3 §2.2; p.9 Future work]
